zh.summary: Granite 正在构建面向 AI 智能体的“Agentic Cloud”，以自持密钥、节点加密和模块化数据中心为卖点，提供从裸金属、GPU、存储、网络、计算到智能体运行时的六层栈。
zh.judgment: 最关键的商业判断是：Granite 押注“智能体工作负载需要主权可控的专用基础设施”这一细分需求，而非在通用云上做一层编排；但官网证据只能证明架构主张与网络规模自述，尚不能证明付费需求或单位经济成立。
zh.replaces: 替代的是在通用公有云上拼装 GPU 实例、对象存储与容器编排，再自行叠加智能体框架的旧做法；也部分替代企业自建机房加第三方云管平台的组合。
zh.segment: 主权可控的 AI 智能体云基础设施（Agentic Cloud），含自有机柜式模块化数据中心与网络化算力服务两条交付路径。
zh.product: 官网把产品拆成六层：Metal（裸金属服务器、路由与电源统一纳管）、GPU（自有与租用 GPU、推理引擎与 AI broker）、Storage（内容寻址文件系统、S3/Redis 兼容对象存储、去重与后量子安全存储 Beta）、Network（Mycelium 覆盖网络，含 DNS、网关、NAT64、GeoIP）、Compute（Mycelium OS 将机器切分为虚拟机、容器或裸金属切片）、Agentic（Hero OS 与智能体编排、记忆、对象）。交付有两种形态：Granite Web Services 直接在网络上消费算力、存储、GPU 与智能体；Granite Infrastructure 则是客户自有的液冷集装箱式单元，部署在客户选定站点。官网称模型无关，可自带开放权重或授权模型，价值主张落在 Hero OS 这一智能体运行层。以上均为公司披露，产品文档需留邮箱获取，实际 API、SLA 与限制未公开。
zh.customer: 使用者推测为需要把智能体跑在受控边界内的团队：对数据驻留、密钥归属和司法辖区有硬约束的企业 IT 与安全负责人，以及需要大量 GPU 但不愿长期绑定单一云厂商的 AI 应用团队。付费者更可能是承担合规与采购责任的基础设施或平台工程部门，而非单个开发者。痛点频率取决于智能体工作负载的持续性与数据敏感度：若只是实验性调用，通用云更省事；若涉及持续推理、私有数据记忆与审计，控制权问题会反复出现。官网未披露任何具名客户、行业分布或采购决策链，因此这一画像属于条件式推断。
zh.workflow: 从输入到交付分两条路径。Web Services 路径：客户提出算力、存储、GPU 与智能体需求，在网络上预订节点或切片，把自带模型接入 Hero OS，由编排器分配记忆与对象存储，数天内可上线；数据存放在客户选定位置，密钥由客户持有。Infrastructure 路径：客户签约后准备场地、供电与冷却，Granite 交付自包含液冷集装箱，合同到投产官网称 4 至 9 个月，单元接入同一网络后可继续使用网络侧服务。两条路径共用 Mycelium OS 这一无状态运行层，节点故障时以小型镜像重启并自动重新入网。官网未说明计费颗粒度、配额审批、迁移工具与支持响应流程，这些是评估实际工作流时必须补齐的环节。
zh.business_model: 官网未公布任何价格、计费单位或合同条款，只给出切片粒度（从 1 核到 64 核）与两种消费方式：按需使用网络算力，或直接购买并拥有硬件单元。可推断的收入结构是“订阅/用量型云服务 + 硬件交付与部署”的混合模式，但这是推断而非披露。单位经济的关键变量在于：模块化单元的资本开支与 4 至 9 个月交付周期能否被足够高的利用率摊薄，以及 750 多个独立节点运营者的分成机制如何设计。官网强调无出网锁定费用，意味着收入不能依赖迁移罚金，必须靠持续用量或硬件毛利。定价页、合同期限、最低消费与 GPU 溢价均缺失，无法判断毛利结构。
zh.traction: 公司披露的网络规模为：750 多个独立节点、40 多个国家、10,896 个 CPU 核心、1,196,055 GB 存储在线，单个集装箱可含 80 块 GPU（10 个 GPU 节点各 8 块）、5,760 TB 存储与 3,000 个智能体。官网称平台已上线并在部署中，首个 Infrastructure 单元将于 2026 年某月发货（月份在抓取文本中被占位符替代）。这些是公司自述，未经审计，也不等于付费采用。缺失的证据包括：付费客户数量与留存、实际利用率、收入、单节点经济性、SLA 达成记录，以及任何第三方性能基准。融资记录本身只说明资金支持，不构成需求验证。
zh.moat: 与通用模型或通用云相比，Granite 的差异不在模型能力，而在架构承诺：节点级加密与客户自持密钥、无状态运行层带来的故障自愈、硬件无关以避免单一厂商锁定、以及把能源与数据中心位置作为一等设计变量。这些若被独立验证，会形成迁移成本与合规叙事上的壁垒；但壁垒成立的条件是：Hero OS 的编排能力确实优于开源智能体框架、网络规模能转化为稳定性能、以及“无人可见全网”的去中心化运营不牺牲可观测性与支持质量。若这些只是营销语言，客户完全可以回到通用云加自建密钥管理，壁垒将迅速消失。
zh.funding_read: 本轮为 400 万欧元、轮次标注为 Other、投资方为 Bifrost Studios，日期为 2026 年 9 月 28 日。这个规模对应的是早期基础设施公司，足以支撑团队扩张与首个集装箱单元的交付，但远不足以自建大规模数据中心，因此更可能用于软件层、网络运营与首批部署。资金用途未披露，不能推断具体分配。下一里程碑应是：首个 Infrastructure 单元按期交付并接入网络、Web Services 出现可核验的付费用量、以及公开可复现的性能与安全验证。轮次为 Other，不应解读为 Seed 或 Series A。
zh.risks: 第一，交付风险：模块化数据中心依赖客户场地、供电与冷却准备，4 至 9 个月周期若延期，会同时拖累收入确认与口碑。第二，需求风险：若智能体工作负载最终仍以通用云上的托管服务为主，主权基础设施的溢价难以成立，网络规模自述也无法转化为付费。第三，运营风险：750 多个独立节点运营者意味着质量、合规与安全责任分散，任何节点被攻破或数据泄露都会冲击“密钥只在你手”的核心承诺。第四，资本风险：硬件交付与网络扩张都吃现金，400 万欧元在重资产模式下容错空间有限。
zh.takeaway: 可借鉴之处在于把“控制权”做成架构属性而非合同条款：密钥归属、数据位置、无出网锁定这些承诺如果能被技术强制，就比写在 SLA 里更有说服力。另一可取做法是同时提供“拥有硬件”和“消费网络”两条入口，让客户可以先小规模试用再迁移到自有部署，降低采购决策门槛。但创业者应从中看到反面：架构叙事必须配可核验的定价、客户案例与性能数据，否则再漂亮的六层栈也难以完成销售。
zh.watch_next: 接下来可验证的指标包括：首个 Infrastructure 单元是否在承诺窗口内交付并公开接入网络的证据；Web Services 是否公布定价页与最低消费；是否出现具名付费客户或可复现的第三方基准；网络节点数与在线核心数是否持续增长而非一次性披露；以及 Hero OS 是否开放文档与 API 供外部测试。若这些仍停留在官网自述，应把 Granite 视为架构主张尚未被市场验证的早期项目。

en.summary: Granite is building an "Agentic Cloud" for AI agents, pitching customer-held keys, node-level encryption and modular data centres across a six-layer stack from bare metal and GPUs to storage, networking, compute and an agent runtime.
en.judgment: The key commercial bet is that agentic workloads need sovereign, purpose-built infrastructure rather than an orchestration layer on top of general-purpose clouds; the available evidence proves architectural claims and self-reported network size, not paid demand or unit economics.
en.replaces: It replaces the common pattern of stitching together GPU instances, object storage and container orchestration on a hyperscaler and then layering an agent framework on top; it also partly replaces enterprise-owned data centres combined with third-party cloud management.
en.segment: Sovereign, controllable AI agent cloud infrastructure (Agentic Cloud), delivered both as a networked compute service and as customer-owned modular container data centres.
en.product: The site describes six layers: Metal (bare-metal servers, routers and power managed as one fleet), GPU (owned and rented GPUs, inference engines and an AI broker), Storage (content-addressed filesystem, S3/Redis-compatible object storage, deduplication and quantum-safe storage in beta), Network (the Mycelium overlay with DNS, gateway, NAT64 and GeoIP), Compute (Mycelium OS slicing machines into VMs, containers or bare metal), and Agentic (Hero OS with orchestration, memory and objects). There are two delivery modes: Granite Web Services for consuming compute, storage, GPUs and agents over the network, and Granite Infrastructure, a liquid-cooled container unit owned by the customer and deployed at a site of their choosing. The site says it is model-agnostic and that value sits in Hero OS, the agent runtime. All of this is company-reported; the product architecture document requires an email, and APIs, SLAs and limits are not public.
en.customer: The inferred users are teams that need agents to run inside a controlled boundary: enterprise IT and security owners with hard constraints on data residency, key custody and jurisdiction, plus AI application teams needing substantial GPU capacity without long-term lock-in to one cloud. The payer is more likely an infrastructure or platform engineering function carrying compliance and procurement responsibility than an individual developer. Pain frequency depends on workload persistence and data sensitivity: experimental API calls are easier on a general cloud, while continuous inference over private data with audit requirements makes control a recurring problem. No named customers, industry mix or buying process are disclosed, so this remains a conditional inference.
en.workflow: There are two paths from input to delivery. On Web Services, a customer specifies compute, storage, GPU and agent needs, reserves nodes or slices on the network, connects their own models to Hero OS, and the orchestrator allocates memory and object storage, with production in days; data stays at the chosen location and keys stay with the customer. On Infrastructure, the customer prepares a pad, power and cooling, Granite delivers a self-contained liquid-cooled container, and the site says contract-to-production takes four to nine months; once connected, the unit joins the same network. Both paths share the stateless Mycelium OS layer, where a failed node reboots from a small image and rejoins automatically. Billing granularity, quota approval, migration tooling and support response processes are not described, and these must be filled in before judging the real workflow.
en.business_model: No prices, billing units or contract terms are published; the site only gives slice granularity (from one core to 64) and two consumption modes: on-demand network capacity, or buying and owning a hardware unit. The inferable revenue structure is a hybrid of usage-based cloud services plus hardware delivery and deployment, but this is inference, not disclosure. Unit economics hinge on whether modular units' capex and four-to-nine-month delivery cycles can be offset by high utilisation, and on how revenue is shared with the 750-plus independent node operators. The site stresses no egress lock-in, meaning revenue cannot rely on migration penalties and must come from sustained usage or hardware margin. Pricing pages, contract terms, minimum commitments and GPU premiums are missing, so gross margin structure cannot be assessed.
en.traction: Company-reported network figures are 750-plus independent nodes, 40-plus countries, 10,896 CPU cores and 1,196,055 GB of storage online, with a single container able to hold 80 GPUs (ten GPU nodes of eight each), 5,760 TB of storage and 3,000 agents. The site says the platform is live and in deployment, with the first Infrastructure unit shipping in a month of 2026 that appears as a placeholder in the captured text. These are self-reported, unaudited and not evidence of paid adoption. Missing evidence includes paying customer counts and retention, actual utilisation, revenue, per-node economics, SLA attainment and any third-party performance benchmark. The funding record itself only shows financial backing, not demand validation.
en.moat: Versus general models or general clouds, Granite's difference is not model capability but architectural commitments: node-level encryption with customer-held keys, a stateless operating layer for self-healing, hardware agnosticism to avoid single-vendor lock-in, and treating energy and data-centre siting as first-class design variables. If independently verified, these create switching costs and a compliance narrative. The moat holds only if Hero OS orchestration genuinely beats open-source agent frameworks, network scale translates into stable performance, and decentralised operation by independent node owners does not sacrifice observability and support quality. If these remain marketing language, customers can return to a general cloud plus their own key management and the moat disappears quickly.
en.funding_read: This round is EUR 4 million, labelled Other, with Bifrost Studios as investor, dated 28 September 2026. That size fits an early-stage infrastructure company: enough to fund team growth and delivery of a first container unit, but far short of building large data centres, so it more plausibly goes to software, network operations and initial deployments. Use of funds is undisclosed and should not be inferred. The next milestones are on-time delivery and network connection of the first Infrastructure unit, verifiable paid usage on Web Services, and publicly reproducible performance and security validation. Because the round is Other, it should not be read as Seed or Series A.
en.risks: First, delivery risk: modular data centres depend on customer site, power and cooling readiness, and a four-to-nine-month cycle slipping would hit both revenue recognition and reputation. Second, demand risk: if agent workloads end up mostly on managed services atop general clouds, the sovereign-infrastructure premium may not hold and self-reported network scale will not convert into payment. Third, operational risk: 750-plus independent node operators disperse quality, compliance and security responsibility, and any compromised node or data breach would undercut the core promise that keys stay with the customer. Fourth, capital risk: hardware delivery and network expansion are cash-hungry, and EUR 4 million leaves limited room for error in an asset-heavy model.
en.takeaway: The transferable idea is making control an architectural property rather than a contract clause: key custody, data location and no-egress-lock-in are more persuasive when technically enforced than when written into an SLA. Offering both "own the hardware" and "consume the network" entry points also lowers procurement friction by letting customers start small and migrate to their own deployment. The counter-lesson is that architectural narrative must be paired with verifiable pricing, customer cases and performance data, or even a well-drawn six-layer stack will struggle to close sales.
en.watch_next: Verifiable next indicators: whether the first Infrastructure unit ships within the promised window with public evidence of network connection; whether Web Services publishes pricing and minimum commitments; whether named paying customers or reproducible third-party benchmarks appear; whether node counts and online cores keep growing rather than being a one-off disclosure; and whether Hero OS opens documentation and APIs for external testing. If these remain website claims, Granite should be treated as an early project whose architecture is not yet market-validated.
